source_read: PMC HTML full text PMC2689518, the NIH author manuscript (NIHMS118643) of Chem Biodivers 2007;4(8):1770-1804, read in full in my own browser tab and saved to my scratch folder (119,095 characters; all sections 1 to 4 and all 189 references; length confirmed in the page). Figures 1 to 6 are reprinted from the author's earlier papers; their legends and the text giving their values were read, the images were not. The manuscript has no abstract and no funding or acknowledgement statement; the author-information panel (affiliation) was read in the page.

claims.overstatement: Minor. (1) 'In 6 men' (statement and magnitude, twice): the review gives the smoking and urine studies as six subjects (N = 6) and never states their sex; 'mostly involved men' rests on the few studies whose participants the review describes as male (eight males given intravenous THC, 20 male volunteers given tritiated THC, 38 males in the hair study), while Wall et al. dosed women and men. (2) 'Urine stayed positive for up to ... 93 days': the review says only that cannabinoids were detectable for 93 days in that person (no cut-off given); 'positive' applies to the 67-day case (above 20 ng/ml by immunoassay). Otherwise the claim keeps to the source's own framing (association by route and frequency, figures second-hand, single small studies) and does not overstate. Doses appear only as study conditions; the closing sentence about people who feel little at first and take more states an evidence gap, not advice.
claims.note: Every number re-found. Parts supported: all smoked, oral, distribution, half-life, blood and urine figures in the statement and magnitude. Parts not supported by this source: the participants' sex in the 6-person studies, and 'positive' for the 93-day case. Further points: (a) the THC half-life is 'greater than 4.1 d' in 2.4.1 but 'ca. 4.1 d' in 3.1.2 and '4.1 d' in 3.1.4; the claim's 'about 4.1 days' follows 3.1.2 and 3.1.4. (b) The 13-day detection followed four cigarettes containing deuterium-labelled THC, not one labelled dose; the review calls the same protocol deuterium-labelled, isotopically labelled and radiolabelled in different places. (c) The 0.86 ng/ml figure (Peat) is a plasma concentration; the review notes that whole-blood concentrations are about half those in plasma, so the claim's heading 'Blood' should read plasma. (d) The lower-dose cigarette is about 16 mg in 2.1.1, about 15.8 mg in 3.2 and about 18 mg in 2.4.2; the claim's 'about 16 or 34 mg' is the 2.1.1 version. (e) The review states that no pharmacokinetic differences between chronic and occasional users have been substantiated and that terminal half-life did not differ between frequent and infrequent users, so 'frequent use with THC staying in the body for days to weeks' reflects accumulated stores and long detection windows, not slower elimination; the claim could say so. (f) The urine figures of 33.7 and 88.6 hours are mean times of the last positive sample, with negatives interspersed; a naive user's urine may be negative by immunoassay within a few hours of one cigarette.

anchors.extracted: Continuous blood sampling during smoking of one cigarette of 1.75% (about 16 mg) or 3.55% (about 34 mg) THC, plus placebo, followed for 7 days; THC detected in plasma from the first puff, with the onset of effects; mean peaks 84.3 ng/ml (range 50 to 129) and 162.2 ng/ml (76 to 267) at 9.0 minutes, before the last puff sequence at 9.8 minutes; N = 6 (sex not stated).

Despite computer-paced puffing, large differences between six individuals from depth of inhalation as they titrated their dose; mean THC about 60% and 20% of peak at 15 and 30 minutes after smoking; 5 ng/ml or less within 2 hours; detectable (limit 0.5 ng/ml) for 3 to 12 hours after the 1.75% and 6 to 27 hours after the 3.55% cigarette.

anchors.locator: 2.1.1. Smoking, 1st paragraph; 2.4.2. Percentage of THC Excreted as Urinary THC-COOH, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Smoked bioavailability 2% to 56%, partly from within- and between-person differences in smoking dynamics (number, length and spacing of puffs, hold time, inhalation volume); elsewhere systemic availability about 8% to 24%, depending strongly on experience with smoking cannabis.

Oral absorption slower, with lower, more delayed peaks; THC in sesame oil (15 mg for women, 20 mg for men) peaked about 4 to 6 hours after ingestion with bioavailability 10% to 20%, by a radiolabel method that could not separate THC from metabolites and overestimated THC; 20 mg in a chocolate cookie gave peaks of 4.4 to 11 ng/ml at 1 to 5 hours and bioavailability about 6% (GC/MS); oral bioavailability summarised as 4% to 20%, owing to variable absorption, degradation in the stomach and first-pass metabolism in the liver to active 11-OH-THC and inactive metabolites.

anchors.locator: 2.1.2. Oral, 3rd and 6th paragraphs; 3.1.3. Oral Administration, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: One 10 mg dronabinol capsule in 17 volunteers: mean peaks THC 3.8 ng/ml (1.1 to 12.7), 11-OH-THC 3.4 (1.2 to 5.6), THC-COOH 26 (14 to 46) at 1 to 2 hours, often with two THC peaks; compared with smoking, onset delayed, peaks lower and effects longer, with a delayed return to baseline; after oral THC, 11-OH-THC higher than THC (Nadulski); oral THC in a cookie gave low and irregular plasma concentrations.

anchors.locator: 2.3.1. Hepatic Metabolism, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs; 3.1.2. Smoked Cannabis, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: 11-OH-THC is equipotent with THC; after smoking it reaches about 10% of THC (6% to 10% for the first 45 minutes, mean peaks 6.7 and 7.5 ng/ml at 13.5 minutes), while after oral THC the two are similar.

anchors.locator: 2.2. Distribution, 1st and 9th paragraphs; 3.1. Plasma Concentrations, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: THC is highly lipophilic, 95% to 99% protein-bound in plasma, mainly to lipoproteins, with a large volume of distribution (about 10 l/kg; 3.4 l/kg at steady state); with prolonged exposure it concentrates in human fat; whole-blood concentrations are about half those in plasma.

anchors.locator: 3.1.2. Smoked Cannabis, 1st paragraph; 3.1.4. Cannabinoid Concentrations after Frequent Use, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Deuterium-labelled THC detected in blood for up to 13 days in people with chronic use who smoked four labelled cigarettes (detection limit 0.02 ng/ml); terminal plasma half-life of THC about 4.1 days in that study against frequent estimates of 24 to 36 hours from studies with less sensitive methods and shorter sampling; in frequent users, plasma THC 0.86 ± 0.22, 11-OH-THC 0.46 and THC-COOH 45.8 ng/ml at least 12 hours after the last smoked dose.

anchors.locator: 2.4.1. Terminal Elimination Half-Lives of THC-COOH, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Short sampling (24 to 72 hours) underestimates terminal half-lives; terminal THC half-life reported as greater than 4.1 days in chronic users; THC-COOH plasma half-life up to 12.6 days in one chronic user monitored for four weeks; mean THC-COOH half-lives 5.2 and 6.2 days for frequent and infrequent users; no pharmacokinetic differences between chronic and occasional users substantiated.

anchors.locator: 3.1.5. Prediction Models for Estimation of Cannabis Exposure, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Plasma THC begins to fall before effects peak; peak effects came when THC and THC-COOH concentrations were equal, 30 to 45 minutes after smoking began; people with frequent use may carry residual plasma THC below 2 ng/ml some 12 hours after smoking.

One person who had used heavily for more than ten years was positive above 20 ng/ml by immunoassay up to 67 days after last use, while a naive user's urine may be negative within a few hours of one cigarette; a positive urine test shows only that exposure occurred, not the route, amount, timing or degree of impairment.

anchors.locator: 3.2.1. THC-COOH Detection Windows in Urine, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: At the 15 ng/ml GC/MS cut-off, the last positive urine sample came a mean of 33.7 ± 9.2 hours (range 8 to 68.5) after one 1.75% cigarette and 88.6 ± 23.2 hours (57 to 122.3) after one 3.55% cigarette; near the cut-off results fluctuate, and three of six subjects had positives interspersed among negatives after the 1.75% cigarette.

anchors.locator: 3.2.2. Normalization of Cannabinoid Urine Concentrations to Urine Creatinine Concentrations, 5th paragraph
anchors.extracted: In one person with heavy use, cannabinoids were detectable in urine for 93 days after stopping, with an excretion half-life of 32 days (cut-off not stated).

Narrative review with no search or selection methods; much of the controlled human data, and all six figures, come from the author's own laboratory (18 of the 189 references name her). Participants' sex is given only for some studies (eight males intravenous, 20 male volunteers tritiated THC, 38 males hair study; women and men in Wall et al.); the 6-subject smoking and urine studies are given without sex.

key_findings.note: Citations checked against references 5 to 9, 13, 17 and 114.

key_findings.correction: Replace '6 men' with '6 participants (N = 6; the review does not state their sex)'. Everything else confirmed at 2.1.1, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs, and the Fig. 1 and 2 legends.

Attribution: the 80% to 90% excreted within 5 days is cited to Harvey (2001) and Halldin et al. (1982) (references 21 and 95); only the split of more than 65% in feces and about 20% in urine is cited to Wall et al. (1983). Also, the 4.1-day study is described as deuterium-labelled in 3.1.2 (as radiolabelled in 3.1.4); rest confirmed.

key_findings.note: The 13-day detection followed four labelled cigarettes.

key_findings.correction: Replace '6 men' with '6 participants (the review says six subjects; sex not stated)'. All numbers confirmed at the stated places.

reporting_issues.note: Recomputed 93.9 µg / 18 mg = 0.52%, / 15.8 mg = 0.59%; 197.4 µg / 34 mg = 0.58%. A mean of individual percentages need not equal the ratio of means, so this alone does not prove an error, but the three dose figures do conflict.

risk_of_bias.note: Editors' narrative-review checklist, overall high: no search or selection criteria and heavy reliance on the author's own studies (18 of 189 references name her, my count), including two conference presentations.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor. All four points verified at the stated places (3.1.5, 3rd paragraph; 3.1.5, 1st paragraph; 2.2, 4th and 6th paragraphs; 3.2, 1st, and 3.2.2, 5th paragraphs).

missed: The '6 men' error also appears in sample.recruitment ('6 men smoking cigarettes of 1.75% and 3.55% THC') and underlies 'small groups of men' in cannot_establish; the review gives sex only for some studies (eight males IV, 20 male volunteers, 38 males in the hair study; women and men in Wall et al.).

The 4.1-day half-life study (Johansson et al. 1988) is described as using deuterium-labelled THC with GC/MS (3.1.2), then as a radiolabelled protocol (3.1.2, same paragraph; 3.1.4) and as isotopically labelled (2.4.1), and its 13-day detection followed four labelled cigarettes.
3.2, 1st paragraph: a naive user's urine may test negative by immunoassay within a few hours after one cigarette; a useful lower bound beside the 67- and 93-day cases.

Minor: interpretation_gap.results_show and exposure.abstinence_at_testing describe the 93-day case as positive urine or urinary THC-COOH; the review says cannabinoids were detectable for 93 days, cut-off not given.

Funding field confirmed: the author-information panel gives the affiliation as Chemistry and Drug Metabolism, Intramural Research Program, NIDA, NIH, Baltimore, and the manuscript has no funding, acknowledgement or conflict statement.
